candidate.answerReason: Two odd primes have an even sum greater than 2, which cannot be prime. Thus one summand is 2, and p<q forces p=2.

methods.label: Use odd and even numbers
methods.explanation: The only even prime is \(2\), because every larger even number has \(2\) as a factor besides \(1\) and itself. If \(p>2\), then \(q>p\) makes both primes odd. Their sum \(r=p+q\) would then be even and greater than \(2\), contradicting that \(r\) is prime. Therefore \(p=2\). These conditions are possible, as \(2+3=5\). The answer is \(\boxed{2}\), choice A.
methods.levelReason: The proof uses only the definition of a prime and elementary parity.
